notes: Page 2 is an introductory illustration (minifigure opening the box and sorting pieces) with no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
The parts list was received with this page and will be used for later build pages.
Page 3, steps 1-2. Step 1: b1 (white 2x6 plate) is the first piece, rests_on []. b2 (white 1x2 plate) sits on b1 at one end: rests_on [b1].
Step 2: b3 (white 2x4 plate) is attached UNDERNEATH b1, offset so it overhangs the left end; b1 therefore rests_on b3 (expressed as joined edges since b1 was already recorded). b3 rests_on [].
The exact overlap (assumed 2 studs/columns) and the stud rows/columns for b2 are estimated from the small illustration.
Page 4, steps 3-4. Step 3: model is flipped over (rotate arrows); b4 (white Technic brick 1x2) is placed at the end of b1 on top of b2 (rests_on [b2]); it spans the width of the plate at the end.

Step 4: two tan Technic 1x1 bricks (b5, b6) each get a black Technic pin (b7, b8) pushed into the pin hole (2x callout), then are placed on b1 beside b4 (rests_on [b1]). White 2x2 brick b9 is placed on b1 next to them (rests_on [b1]).

Exact stud positions (b1 columns 3-5) are inferred from the small illustration; the pin-hole direction is sideways. Earlier b2 stud mapping to b1 (1.5/1.6) may really be the end column across both rows.

Page 5, step 5: two more tan Technic 1x1 bricks (b12, b13) each receive a black pin (b10, b11), then are placed on b1 at the other end of the white 2x2 brick b9 (rests_on [b1]). The white inverted 2x2 slope (b14, lego-3660 is the only white 2x2 slope in the parts list) is assumed to sit on the exposed 2x2 studs of b3 beyond the end of b1 (rests_on [b3]); its placement is not clearly drawn.
Step 6: the callout shows a white 1x2 plate and a white 2x6 plate, but the page only shows the model before they are placed. They are deferred to the next page where the placement is drawn.
All stud positions are inferred from small illustrations.

Page 6 shows only the step 7 callout (a white 2x2 brick and a white 3x2 33° slope) over the model as it stands after step 6; the step 7 pieces are not yet placed on this page, so they are deferred to the next page.

Recorded here the two step 6 pieces from the previous page's callout (white 2x6 plate b15 and white 1x2 plate b16), inferred from the model drawn. b15 is assumed to lie across the tops of the Technic bricks (b12, b13, b5, b6, b4) and the 2x2 brick b9. The position of b16 (placed on the end of b15) is a low-confidence guess.
The drawing is small and ambiguous; the placement of the b14 inverted slope may differ from my earlier assumption.
Page 7: step 8 adds a white 1x2 plate (b19) and a light-grey 2x2 plate with side studs (b20); step 9 adds a light-grey 2x2 plate (b21) on top of b20.

Step 7 pieces (white 2x2 brick b17 and white 3x2 33° slope b18) are drawn as placed in the model pictures on this page (they appeared in the page 6 callout), so they are recorded here: both rest on the top plate b15; the slope b18 is assumed to overhang the rear end of b15.
Stud positions on b15 and the layout at the head end (b16, b19, b20, b21) are inferred from small, ambiguous drawings and may be off by a column.
The earlier assumed placement of the inverted slope b14 remains uncertain.

Page 8 starts a new sub-assembly (the sheep's head, shown in the inset at top): step 1 light-grey 2x4 plate b22 (first piece, rests_on []); step 2 light-grey 2x2 plate with side studs b23 (lego-99206) on one end of b22, side studs facing outward.

Correction: the parts list has only one lego-99206, which is used here. The grey part I recorded as b20 on page 7 (step 8) was probably the Plate Special 1x2 with side handle (lego-48336), not lego-99206. This cannot be edited retroactively.
Studs used on b22 (end 2x2) are inferred from the drawing.
Page 9, head sub-assembly. Step 3: two light-grey 1x1 bricks with side stud (b24, b25) and a light-grey 1x2 30° slope (b26). Step 4: white 3x2 33° slope (b27).

Positions are inferred from small drawings: b24/b25 on b22 in the third column (one in each row), side studs facing outward; b26 on the raised studs of b23; b27 covers b24, b25 and the last column of b22 and overhangs the end of the plate.
The step 3 drawing is ambiguous about which 1x1 goes where (only one shown in the inset), so stud assignments are approximate.

Page 10, head sub-assembly. Step 5 (2x): two dark round 1x1 plates (assumed lego-6141 Dark Bluish Gray, the ears) are attached sideways onto the side studs of the two 1x1 side-stud bricks b24 and b25; they clutch nothing below, so rests_on is empty and they are recorded as joined edges to the side studs.
Step 6: white 2x2 plate b30 on top of the head, assumed to sit on the 1x2 slope b26 and the free studs of b23. The exact supporting studs are inferred from the drawing.

Page 11, step 7 (head): two black horns (lego-87747) and two white eye tiles (lego-98138pr0008). The eye tiles go on the side studs of the 1x1 side-stud bricks b24/b25 (the eyes sit on the sides of the head); the horns clip into the two dark clip pieces placed in step 5.

CORRECTION to page 10: the two dark pieces of step 5 (b28, b29) are almost certainly Plate Special 1x1 with Clip (lego-4081b, black, 2x in the parts list), not lego-6141 round plates, and they sit on the two raised studs of the white slope b27 (edges added now), not on the side studs of b24/b25. Disregard the earlier b28/b29 to b24/b25 side-stud edges. Their type could not be changed retroactively; the horn edges use port 'clip.1' for that reason.
The step 10 picture on this page is only a preview showing the finished head attached to the body (the large body sub-assembly); no placement is added from it now.
Page 12, step 11 (nose): light-grey 1x1 plate with horizontal clip (b35) goes on the front side stud of the head plate b23; the bright pink 1x1 groove tile (b36) goes on its stud (the pink nose).

The drawing already shows the head sub-assembly attached to the body. That join (the 'step 10' preview on page 11) was not recorded earlier, so it is added here: the head base plate b22 sits on the front 2x2 plate b21 of the body. Which studs are used is inferred.
The side stud on b23 used for the nose is assumed to be stud.side.1.

Page 13, step 12 (2x): builds two legs, each: foot slope (dark grey 2x1 cutout slope) -> dark 1x1 plate -> light-grey 1x1 brick -> white inverted 2x1 slope -> white Technic 1x2 brick -> white 1x2 30° slope on top.

Legs are then pushed onto the body's black Technic pins by the Technic brick's pin hole (arrow to the body). Two legs shown on the near side; I assume they use the pins b10 (front) and b7 (rear) on one side of the body, and that the other two legs are made in a later step (the parts list has 4 of each leg part).
The inverted slope 3665 has studs on its flat top in reality, but the catalogue lists only anti-studs for it; stud.1.1/stud.1.2 are used for it anyway.
Which pins carry which legs depends on drawing orientation; guessed.

Page 14, step 13 (2x): the same leg sub-assembly as step 12 is built twice more (the page shows the same part set, with the foot slope drawn from the other side). The model is turned over (rotate arrow) and these two legs go onto the opposite side of the body, onto the black Technic pins b11 (front) and b8 (rear) in the tan bricks b13 and b6.
The pins/side assignment is inferred; the step 12 legs were assumed on b10 and b7. This completes the four legs (the parts list has 4 of each leg part).
As before, the inverted slope uses stud.1.1/stud.1.2 although the catalogue lists only anti-studs.
Page 15, step 14: a light-grey Technic pin 1/2 (b37) is pushed into the pin hole at the rear end of the body (the white Technic brick b4), forming the tail mount.

Step 15: the callout shows one white 1x2 plate, but the drawing shows no clearly visible placement (the pictured model looks unchanged apart from the rear), so it is deferred to the next page where it can be placed.

Page 16 starts a new sub-assembly: the base/diorama (brown ground with green grass and a tan hill, shown in the top inset). Step 1: reddish brown 4x6 plate b38 (first piece of this sub-assembly, rests_on []).

Step 2: three reddish brown 2x2 double-convex slopes (1x + 2x in the callout). Two are assumed side by side across the width at one end of b38 (columns 5-6), and the third beside them (columns 3-4, rows 1-2). The drawing is ambiguous, so the placements are guesses.
The sheep model built on earlier pages is a separate sub-assembly; the step 15 white 1x2 plate from page 15 is still unplaced.

Page 17, step 3: blue 2x4 brick b42 (the water/pond) placed on the brown base plate b38 next to the slopes. It is assumed to cover rows 3-4, columns 1-4 of b38; the drawing is ambiguous and it might also touch the slopes.

Page 18, step 4: a second reddish brown 4x6 plate (b43). The drawing shows the base with blue brick and slopes sitting on a larger plate with studs visible all around, so b43 is interpreted as lying UNDER b38 (b38 rests on b43), offset so studs of b43 remain visible. b43 is recorded with no rests_on; the join is given as edges from b38's anti-studs to b43's studs.

The amount and position of the overlap is a guess (assumed a 2x2 overlap in the middle); it could be a larger overlap. Alternatively the plate could be on top of the assembly, but the picture shows the blue brick uncovered.
Page 19: step 5 (2x) and step 6 (2x) each add two reddish brown 2x4 45° slopes (b44, b45 near side; b46, b47 far side), forming the hillside around the blue pond brick b42.

The base layout is very ambiguous: slopes are recorded as resting on the lower plate b43 on free studs, with partial overlap edges only. The real layout (and whether they also rest on b38 or the blue brick) is uncertain; the exact studs are guesses.

Page 20, step 7: third reddish brown 4x6 plate (b48). The picture shows the hill with its pond on a longer plate base, so b48 is interpreted as a plate under b43 that extends the base, with a small overlap (assumed a 2x2 overlap). b48 itself rests_on [].
Overlap and position are guesses from a small, ambiguous drawing.

Page 21, step 8: three reddish brown 2x2 slopes: 1x (taken as the fourth lego-3045, double convex) and 2x (taken as lego-3039 reddish brown, the only other 2x2 brown slopes in the parts list). They form the sloped end/corners of the hill on the third plate b48.

Placement is a guess: b49 at b48 columns 3-4 rows 1-2, b50 at columns 5-6 rows 1-2, b51 at columns 5-6 rows 3-4. The 2x2 slopes only have two anti ports listed for 3039, so only two edges each for b50/b51.
The page 16 step 2 callout pieces may include a different mix of 3045/3039; ids kept as recorded.
Page 22, step 9: three green 2x2 grooved tiles (3068b) and two green 1x2 jumper plates with one stud (15573 – the icon shows a 1x2 plate with one stud) form the grass patch at one end of the hill.

Which slopes carry which grass pieces is very uncertain from the small drawing; the pieces are recorded as resting on slope studs (b50, b51, b47 for tiles; b46, b45 for jumpers). The hill layout assumptions from earlier pages already contain guesses.
Page 23, step 10 (2x): two green 2x6 plates (b57, b58) side by side cover the rest of the hill top and the blue pond brick, forming the grass surface next to the grass tiles from step 9.
Support points (slopes b46/b44 and the blue brick b42) are guessed from the small drawing.

Page 24, step 11: tan 2x2 slope (b59) and a light-grey 1x1 brick (b60) at the left end of the green plates. Step 12: two tan 2x1 slopes with bottom pin (b61, b62) either side of the hill, one dark round 1x1 plate (b63) and two light-grey round 1x1 plates (b64, b65) as rocks on top.

Stud positions are guesses from small drawings; the round plates are assumed to be lego-6141 (dark bluish gray and light bluish gray), as in the parts list. The slopes with bottom pin are shown with only two anti ports in the catalogue, used as such.

Page 25, step 13 (2x): two dark round 1x1 plates (b66, b67) are stacked onto the dark round plate b63 on the hill, forming a tall stack of rocks. Step 14: a tan 1x1 cheese slope (b68) and a green bamboo plant (b69) on the green plate in front of the hill.
Exact stud positions are guessed from small drawings.

Page 26, step 15: two tan slopes (the callout icons look like small slopes; by the parts count they are the two remaining lego-3040b 2x1 pin slopes, since both 54200 cheese slopes are accounted for by steps 14 and 16) plus one light-grey round 1x1 plate (the last lego-6141 light bluish gray). Step 16: tan cheese slope (second lego-54200) and a second green bamboo plant on top of the hill.
Positions are guesses from small drawings.

Page 27 is the finished model view: the sheep (head, body, four legs) stands on the grass base. The feet are recorded as joined to the green plates b57/b58 (one stud each, positions guessed; leg1/leg2/legb1/legb2 foot ids come from the repeat copies on pages 13 and 14).

Also recorded here is the white 1x2 plate left unplaced from page 15 step 15 (b75); its position was not clearly drawn, so it is assumed to sit on the studs of the rear slope b18 as a tail tip. This is a guess.
No new building steps are shown on this page; the sheep-to-base attachment is deduced from the final picture.
Page 28 is the parts inventory / customer service page with no building step, so it adds nothing.
Many placements across the build (especially the base plates and slopes on pages 16-26 and the earlier head/body join) were inferred from small drawings and may need review.

Inventory fix: the parts list has only one lego-99206 (b23, the head base plate) and one lego-48336. The grey piece b20 (page 7, step 8) is re-declared as lego-48336 (Plate Special 1x2 side handle), replacing its earlier lego-99206 type. Its old edges that used ports it does not have (anti.2.x, stud.2.x) should be disregarded; the corrected joins are b20 on b16 and b21 resting on b20 (stud.1.1/1.2) plus b19.

The two dark clip pieces b28/b29 (page 10, step 5) are re-declared as lego-4081b (Plate Special 1x1 with Clip Light, black x2), replacing lego-6141. They sit on the raised studs of b27 (edges already given); the earlier edges from b28/b29 to the side studs of b24/b25 should be disregarded. This also leaves the 6141 count at 6 (3 LBG: b64, b65, b72; 3 DBG: b63, b66, b67), matching the list.
Added the 2015 Year Of The Sheep envelope (lego-6116050, b76). It is a separate item in the box (the red-packet gift) and is not built into the model, so it has no joins.
Positions of b16/b19/b20/b21 at the sheep's front end are still inferred from small drawings.

Inventory: re-declaring existing ids with a new type was ignored, so the correct pieces are added with NEW ids: b77 = lego-48336 (the grey side-handle plate), b78 and b79 = lego-4081b (the two black clip plates that hold the horns). These REPLACE the mis-typed b20 (lego-99206 → really the 48336), b28 and b29 (lego-6141 → really the two 4081b). b20, b28, b29 and every edge that uses them (including the old b28/b29 side-stud joins to b24/b25) should be dropped; the build is otherwise unchanged. After dropping them the counts match the parts list: one 99206 (b23), one 48336 (b77), two 4081b (b78, b79), six 6141 (b64, b65, b72, b63, b66, b67).

Connectivity: the envelope (lego-6116050, b76) is a loose gift item in the box, not built into either model. It is given a 'contact' edge to the base plate b43 (it simply rests beside it in the box) so the graph is one group. The sheep and the base are joined by the feet edges (leg1/leg2/legb1/legb2 .foot to b57/b58) because the finished model stands on the base.
Positions of the front-end plates and the clip plates are inferred from small drawings.
